title: Cross-Corridor Conversion: From Authorization To Operation
summary: Compare authorization and operating transitions with named carrier service panels while keeping networks, schedules, causes, safety, accessibility, and local outcomes separate.
current_state_summary: United, Southwest, and Delta now have two-year operating-carrier cancellation panels with scheduled-flight denominators preserved.
current_state: Northern Virginia has load, rate, transmission, permit, and water rails; final route, construction, energization, customer service, use, and reliability remain incomplete.

Nevada has federal land decisions, state permits, and a closed Thacker Pass loan; condition satisfaction, construction, commissioning, qualification, output, sales, and environmental performance remain incomplete.

Florida has master plans, site licensing, environmental decisions, operator rules, and capital channels; named project funding, construction, acceptance, mission authorization, utilization, and outcomes remain incomplete.
Florida now has an operational access bridge and one completed active-countdown resilience operation, but mission licensing and measured system outcomes remain incomplete.
Research Watches 001 and 002 and Local Authorization Is Not Operation expose the shared stage-conversion problem without treating the corridors as legally or technically equivalent.
USGS 2025 commodity data and FAA national operation counts provide operating comparators without resolving named Nevada or Florida project outcomes.
Four mobility and mission series supply context without converting national activity into local readiness or outcome claims.
DOT Table 6C supports within-carrier 2024-2025 cancellation reads without authorizing its cross-carrier ranking frame.
Phase 56C adds entity-matched controls, inputs, constraints, later observations, attribution, independent-validation limits, and alternative explanations.
Temporal order is preserved without converting association into causation, ranking, composite scoring, or readiness scoring.
Phase 56D adds later observations and explicit tests of named Phase 56C alternative explanations for the same twelve entities.
Compatibility, attribution, validation status, missing denominators, and series breaks remain visible before any interpretation.
Phase 56E adds a second vertically replicated cohort: American Airlines, Alaska Airlines, JetBlue Airways.
Every retained entity carries a panel, a driver-and-constraint dossier, and an alternative-explanation test under one stable identity.
Phase 56F assigns every entity one highest-value missing record, one strongest compatible current record, a closure state, and an explicit reopening rule.
Across all 24 entities, one bounded record is Closed, sixteen are Partially Closed, and seven remain Open; these are evidence states, not performance measures.
Phase 56I completes 6 first-pass decisions in this pathway while retaining each coverage ID and continuation rule.
No selected closure state changes; genuinely new denominators publish and repeated evidence remains referenced rather than relabeled as a new finding.

dependency_stack.current_state: Each corridor has named upstream records that establish demand, rules, plans, permits, environmental decisions, or financing stages.
dependency_stack.boundary: The instruments differ and none alone proves a completed, accepted, operating, or scaled asset.

dependency_stack.current_state: Named projects have partial construction, permitting, route, finance, environmental, inspection, assurance, testing, and service trails; Kennedy's causeway bridge closes one physical delivery stage.
dependency_stack.boundary: Partial trails do not establish that all conditions were satisfied, assets were built and accepted, or compliance was sustained.

dependency_stack.current_state: The next decisive records differ by corridor: customer service, qualified material output, or authorized mission use.
dependency_stack.boundary: Projected demand, output, or launch cadence cannot stand in for delivered service, accepted products, or completed missions.

dependency_stack.current_state: One Kennedy operating adaptation is documented, but no corridor record set supports a complete claim about sustained capacity, cost, reliability, safety, environmental performance, or local outcomes.
dependency_stack.boundary: Scale requires sustained operating evidence and measured receiving-system results.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve national mobility and mission observations provide separate service, exposure, operation, and activity rails.
dependency_stack.boundary: Flights, cancellations, test miles, licensed operations, missions, and local utilization use different denominators.

dependency_stack.current_state: Three reporting operating carriers now have named two-year cancellation panels.
dependency_stack.boundary: Cancellation rates do not share network, schedule mix, airport, weather, cause, customer, safety, accessibility, or local-effect context.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve dossiers order baseline, intervention or input, constraint, and later observation.
dependency_stack.boundary: Temporal sequence and attribution do not establish causal effect.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve entity tests map later records to named competing explanations.
dependency_stack.boundary: A test may narrow an explanation without isolating cause or producing a score.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve additional entities passed a four-primary-record screen and received all three evidence layers.
dependency_stack.boundary: Entity depth can increase without making different entities comparable.

dependency_stack.current_state: One selected record and one reopening rule now govern each of the 24 named entities.
dependency_stack.boundary: Closed, Partially Closed, and Open describe the selected evidence question only; they do not compare entity performance.

dependency_stack.current_state: Every remaining Open and Partially Closed queue item has a dated decision; two genuinely new bounded denominators publish.
dependency_stack.boundary: A first-pass decision, monthly record, program commitment, or current source check is not full closure or entity performance.

evidence_limits: The pathway compares evidence stages, not economic, environmental, institutional, or technical equivalence.
A rate decision, mining permit, federal loan, site license, environmental decision, and master plan are not interchangeable.
No pathway record establishes corridor-wide readiness, spare capacity, qualified output, mission availability, or accepted local outcomes.
National commodity and commercial-space operating baselines do not close project-level construction, qualification, mission, utilization, or local-outcome gates.
National series cannot establish a named corridor's readiness, service, safety, accessibility, cost, or local benefit.
Operating-carrier rows must remain separate from marketing-carrier networks and branded code-share partners.
Two observations do not establish a durable trend.
A named intervention, control, input, or response does not by itself explain an observed outcome.
Company and operator claims remain attributed until independently validated.
A recommendation status, certification, supplier clause, incident response, monthly cause mix, or complaint count does not create a common performance measure.
Different units, methods, identities, observation windows, and attribution levels remain split.
The second cohort preserves attribution, unit, denominator, method, observation window, reporting breaks, and identity changes.
A vertical entity record does not authorize cross-entity ranking, composite scoring, readiness scoring, or causal inference.
Phase 56F closure states apply to one named missing record per entity and cannot be converted into a ranking, composite, readiness score, or causal claim.
Phase 56I first-pass and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
